parsed.rationale: All 11 members are unnamed `extension` declarations on `EnvironmentValues` spread across 5 distinct packages (AppServices, Playback, WXUI, Wallpaper, PlayerHeaderView). The SwiftUI pattern of extending `EnvironmentValues` in the file that defines the corresponding key is idiomatic and intentional — each extension adds domain-specific keys local to its package (e.g., `PlaylistServiceEnvironment.swift`, `AccentColorEnvironment.swift`, `RadioPlayerControllerEnvironment.swift`). The structural collision is purely nominal: every file that adds a SwiftUI environment key must extend `EnvironmentValues`, so the name collision is an artifact of the SwiftUI API contract, not a sign of duplicated logic. No fields or method signatures are shared (`fields_or_signature: []` on every record), and no restraint markers are present, but consolidating these extensions would couple unrelated packages and violate the single-responsibility principle each file currently upholds.
